summary: Bo Jiang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jiang earned a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2008) under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.
Bo-gwang Han specializes in Buddhist studies and held a professorship at Dongguk University (attested 2004, 2015). Han also taught Silwon Suk.

Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989). He held a post at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery (~1984–2004) and taught Shenpen Hookham and Lama Palden Drolma.

Bong Seok Joo works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley, where teachers included Lewis Lancaster, and earned a PhD from Princeton University under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and teacher Jacqueline I. Stone.

Bongkil Chung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Chung earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts at Florida International University, serving in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1923–1928) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1928–1937).

Brad Warner (born 1964) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who attended Wadsworth High School and Kent State University. He studied under traditional teacher Tim McCarthy (~1983) and teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima (attested 2017).

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Phillips studied at Naropa University, earned a B.A. (1989) and PhD (2004) under David Germano at the University of Virginia, and earned an M.T.S. from Harvard University (1993).
Bradley L. Herling specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad (~1939–1943). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and a habilitation at LMU Munich, later holding posts at SOAS (~2006–2010) and LMU Munich (~2010–2018).
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in religious studies. Harwood earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under advisor Patrick Pranke.

Brendan S. Gillon specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984) and served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University (~1992).

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, held research posts at Otani and Kyoto, taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin, and served as a philosophy professor at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.

Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor of Japanese Studies.

Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple University (PhD 1991), later holding posts at Antioch University (~2005–2013) and the University of Adelaide (attested 2011).
Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under doctoral supervisor György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, and Haileybury. He served as Assistant Resident (1820) and Resident (~1833–1843) at the Court of Nepal and British Residency.

Brian J. Nichols specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and completed a PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Anne Carolyn Klein.
